name: Light Roast
description: Roasted just past the first audible crack of the bean, stopping before much roast flavor develops. Lets the coffee's origin character — its acidity and fruit or floral notes — come through most clearly.

name: Medium Roast
description: A balance point between origin character and roast character. The most common roast level for pour-over and drip brewing.

name: Dark Roast
description: Roasted well past second crack, developing bold roast flavors that dominate over the bean's origin character. Beans often show a visible sheen of oil on the surface.
